report.title: Anthropic and PwC expand alliance: 30,000 staff certified on Claude Code
report.summary: PwC will roll out Claude Code and Claude Cowork to its full global workforce of 364,000, starting with 30,000 US professionals, and is launching a Claude-native finance group inside its CFO practice. Production deployments are already live: insurance underwriting cycles cut from 10 weeks to 10 days, incident response from hours to minutes.

report.title: OpenAI rolls GPT-5.5 Instant to all ChatGPT users as new default model
report.summary: GPT-5.5 Instant replaces GPT-5.3 Instant as the default across ChatGPT and as chat-latest in the API, shipping adjustable reasoning effort levels (minimal through xhigh) and better tone control for voice and text agents. GPT-5.3 stays available for paid users for three months before retirement.

report.title: OpenAI ships GPT-Realtime-2, GPT-Realtime-Translate, and GPT-Realtime-Whisper
report.summary: Three new realtime audio models drop: GPT-Realtime-2 handles live voice reasoning and tool calls mid-conversation; GPT-Realtime-Translate does speech-to-speech across 70+ input languages into 13 outputs in real time; GPT-Realtime-Whisper streams live transcription. Builders targeting voice-native products now have a full audio stack from one provider.

report.title: Microsoft ships MDASH: agentic multi-model scanner hits 96-100% recall on real CVEs
report.summary: Microsoft's Autonomous Code Security team released MDASH into private preview, a multi-model agentic harness that scored 96% recall on five years of MSRC-confirmed bugs in clfs.sys and 100% on tcpip.sys. It moves AI vulnerability research from research novelty to production-scale enterprise security auditing.

report.title: Google announces Gemini Intelligence for Android and Googlebook laptops
report.summary: Ahead of Google I/O (May 19-20), Google pre-announced Gemini Intelligence — proactive agentic AI baked into Android and ChromeOS — and a new Googlebook laptop lineup from Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, and Lenovo launching this fall with Gemini at the core. Gemini also ships broadly in Android Auto with hands-free DoorDash ordering.

report.title: Claude Code ships background agent persistence, rewind compression, and new env vars
report.summary: A batch of Claude Code CLI updates landed: background agents launched via /bg now preserve permission mode instead of reverting to default, a new 'Summarize up to here' rewind option compresses earlier context, and CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_PREFER_HTTPS lets teams clone GitHub plugins over HTTPS in keyless environments.

report.title: Anthropic overtakes OpenAI in business AI adoption per Ramp spend data
report.summary: Ramp's May AI Index shows Claude at 34.4% business adoption in April vs OpenAI at 32.3%, a reversal in a market OpenAI previously dominated. Claude Code is cited as the primary driver of the share shift.

learn.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
learn.oneLineDescription: Terminal-native coding agent with persistent goals, AWS Bedrock, and MCP support.

detail.whatItDoes:
Codex CLI is an open-source, Rust-built coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally in your terminal. It can read, edit, and execute code in your repo, run tests, spawn sub-agents, and now persist high-level /goal workflows across sessions — meaning you can assign an objective, close your laptop, and resume where it left off. The May 2026 release ships GPT-5.4 as the default model, adding native computer-use and experimental 1M context support.

The CLI connects to Codex Cloud for parallel cloud sandboxes, supports MCP servers for third-party tool integrations, and has a plugin marketplace for extending agent behavior. AWS Bedrock is now a first-class model provider with SigV4 auth, making it practical for teams that already route everything through AWS.
detail.whoItsFor: Engineers who want a terminal-first agentic coding workflow and aren't locked into Cursor or VS Code. Particularly useful for teams on AWS (Bedrock support), shops that want to script headless Codex runs in CI/CD via `codex exec`, and solo builders who want long-running background coding tasks that survive laptop restarts.
pros: Persistent /goal workflows survive session restarts — no babysitting long-running agent tasks
First-class AWS Bedrock support with SigV4 signing, no proxy required
MCP integration lets you wire in any third-party tool or context source
Open-source (Rust) with active weekly releases and a public changelog
Works across macOS, Linux, and Windows (native PowerShell or WSL2)
cons: Requires a ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise plan or API key — not free for heavy use
No hard spending cap tied to /goal workflows; runaway loops burn tokens until plan-level limits kick in
GPT-5.4 computer-use is still experimental; don't rely on it for production automation yet
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Node 20+ (`node --version`)
- A ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise account **or** an OpenAI API key (`OPENAI_API_KEY`)
- macOS, Linux, or Windows with PowerShell / WSL2

## Install

```bash
# Option A: npm (recommended — gets the latest release)
npm install -g @openai/codex

# Option B: Homebrew (macOS)
brew install --cask codex

# Verify
codex --version
```

## First run

```bash
# Navigate to your repo
cd ~/my-project

# Launch interactively — you'll be prompted to sign in on first run
codex
```

Authenticate with your ChatGPT account or paste your API key when prompted. The key is stored in `~/.codex/config.toml`.

## Try a /goal (persistent workflow)

```bash
# Inside the Codex TUI, type:
/goal Write unit tests for all exported functions in src/utils.ts

# Codex persists this goal. Close the terminal, come back later:
codex
/resume
# Pick the goal from the list to continue where it left off
```

## Wire in AWS Bedrock

```toml
# ~/.codex/config.toml
[model_providers.bedrock]
type = "bedrock"
aws_profile = "my-aws-profile"   # matches ~/.aws/credentials profile name
region = "us-east-1"
```

```bash
# Then select a Bedrock model in the TUI, or:
codex --provider bedrock --model anthropic.claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219-v1:0
```

## Add an MCP server

```bash
# Example: add agentmemory for cross-session memory
codex mcp add agentmemory -- npx -y @agentmemory/mcp
```

## Headless / CI mode

```bash
# Run a single task non-interactively (exits when done)
codex exec "Add JSDoc comments to every exported function in src/"

# Report reasoning-token usage as JSON (useful for cost tracking)
codex exec --json "Refactor auth.ts to use async/await"
```

## Gotcha
`codex exec` no longer shows a "research preview" banner — it's production-ready. But if you don't see GPT-5.4 in the model selector, run `codex update` first to get the latest binary.

learn.name: agentmemory
learn.oneLineDescription: MCP-native persistent memory server for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, and any MCP client.

detail.whatItDoes:
agentmemory runs a local Node.js server that silently captures what your coding agent does, compresses sessions into a searchable knowledge store (semantic + BM25 hybrid search), and injects the right context at the start of each new session. It exposes 51 MCP tools (memory_smart_search, memory_save, memory_recall, etc.) and plugs into Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and any other MCP-compatible client via a single `npx` command.

Under the hood it uses SQLite for state, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for local embeddings (no API key required), and a knowledge graph for entity relationships. A real-time viewer UI runs at localhost:3113, showing session replays, memory timelines, and a governance audit trail. The project self-describes as the #1 persistent memory solution for AI coding agents based on real-world benchmarks — claims backed by published LONGMEMEVAL and comparison benchmarks in the repo.
detail.whoItsFor: Anyone using Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, or Gemini CLI for non-trivial engineering work where context loss across sessions costs time. Especially useful for long-running projects where the agent needs to remember architectural decisions, recurring bugs, and team conventions without cramming them into a 200-line CLAUDE.md file.
pros: Zero external databases — runs entirely local with SQLite and a local embedding model
Works with any agent that speaks MCP or HTTP; one server serves all agents simultaneously
Session replay viewer lets you scrub through past agent runs like a debugger
No API key needed for embeddings — uses local all-MiniLM-L6-v2
Actively maintained with weekly releases; 5k+ GitHub stars and growing
cons: Still pre-1.0 (v0.9.x) — the changelog is full of meaningful bug fixes, including a search regression in v0.9.5 fixed in v0.9.6
Single maintainer project; governance plan exists but execution depends on one person
Sandboxed MCP clients (Flatpak, Snap, restrictive containers) need extra env var config to reach localhost
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Node 18+ (`node --version`)
- Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible agent already installed

## Start the memory server

```bash
# Terminal 1 — keep this running
npx @agentmemory/agentmemory

# Verify it's up
curl http://localhost:3111/agentmemory/health
# Should return: {"status":"ok",...}

# Optional: open the real-time viewer
open http://localhost:3113
```

## Wire into Claude Code

```bash
# Inside Claude Code, run:
/plugin marketplace add rohitg00/agentmemory
/plugin install agentmemory
# This registers 12 hooks, 4 skills, and auto-wires the MCP server
```

## Wire into Codex CLI

```bash
# One-liner MCP registration
codex mcp add agentmemory -- npx -y @agentmemory/mcp

# Or manually in ~/.codex/config.toml:
# [mcp_servers.agentmemory]
# type = "local"
# command = ["npx", "-y", "@agentmemory/mcp"]
# enabled = true
```

## Wire into Cursor or Gemini CLI

Add to your MCP config JSON (location varies by client):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "agentmemory": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@agentmemory/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Seed and test recall

```bash
# Seeds 3 realistic sessions and runs semantic searches against them
npx @agentmemory/agentmemory demo
```

## Import existing Claude Code session history

```bash
# Import all JSONL transcripts under ~/.claude/projects
npx @agentmemory/agentmemory import-jsonl
```

## Gotcha
If you're on v0.9.5 and `memory_smart_search` returns empty results for memories you saved with `memory_save`, upgrade immediately — this was a known regression fixed in v0.9.6: `npx @agentmemory/agentmemory@latest`.

learn.name: Gemini API: Veo 3.1 Lite + Lyria 3
learn.oneLineDescription: Google's new cost-efficient video gen and full-length music generation models, live in the Gemini API.

detail.whatItDoes:
Google's May 2026 Gemini API update ships two new generative media models builders can call directly. Veo 3.1 Lite (`veo-3.1-lite-generate-preview`) is the most cost-efficient video generation model in the Veo family, designed for high-volume applications and rapid iteration — it now supports 4K output resolution and portrait video in all resolutions. Lyria 3 ships in two variants: `lyria-3-clip-preview` for 30-second clips and `lyria-3-pro-preview` for full-length songs, making it the first GA-track music generation API from a major frontier lab.

Both are available via the standard Gemini API and Vertex AI. The same update also launched Flex and Priority inference tiers, letting you trade latency for cost on any Gemini model call — Flex is cheaper for batch/async workloads, Priority is for latency-sensitive production paths.
detail.whoItsFor: Builders adding generative video or music to products — marketing tools, creative apps, social media automation, game asset pipelines. Also relevant for any team already using the Gemini API who wants to optimize inference costs with the new Flex tier rather than switching providers.
pros: Lyria 3 Pro generates full-length songs via API — first from a major lab at this quality level
Veo 3.1 Lite adds 4K and portrait video support, useful for mobile-first apps
Flex/Priority tiers let you tune cost vs. latency on existing Gemini model calls without code changes
All three features available on Vertex AI for enterprise data residency requirements
cons: Both Veo 3.1 Lite and Lyria 3 are still in preview — not GA, subject to breaking changes
Video generation latency is still measured in seconds-to-minutes; not suitable for real-time interactive use cases
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- A Google Cloud project with billing enabled
- Gemini API key from [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/) **or** a Vertex AI service account
- Python 3.9+ with `google-genai` SDK

## Install the SDK

```bash
pip install google-genai
```

## Generate a short video with Veo 3.1 Lite

```python
import google.generativeai as genai
import os, time

genai.configure(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"])

client = genai.Client()

# Start async video generation
operation = client.models.generate_videos(
    model="veo-3.1-lite-generate-preview",
    prompt="A timelapse of a city skyline at dusk, portrait orientation, 4K",
    config={
        "number_of_videos": 1,
        "duration_seconds": 8,
        "aspect_ratio": "9:16",   # portrait
        "resolution": "4k",
    }
)

# Poll until done
while not operation.done:
    time.sleep(10)
    operation = client.operations.get(operation)

for video in operation.response.generated_videos:
    print(video.video.uri)  # download or embed this URI
```

## Generate a music clip with Lyria 3

```python
import google.generativeai as genai
import os

genai.configure(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"])
client = genai.Client()

# 30-second clip
response = client.models.generate_audio(
    model="lyria-3-clip-preview",
    prompt="Upbeat lo-fi hip hop, 90 BPM, warm Rhodes piano, light vinyl crackle",
)
with open("clip.mp3", "wb") as f:
    f.write(response.audio_data)

# Full-length song (lyria-3-pro-preview)
response = client.models.generate_audio(
    model="lyria-3-pro-preview",
    prompt="Cinematic orchestral intro building to a full ensemble, 3 minutes",
)
with open("song.mp3", "wb") as f:
    f.write(response.audio_data)
```

## Use Flex tier to cut costs on batch workloads

```python
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-3.1-pro-preview",
    contents="Summarize this 50-page document: ...",
    config={"inference_tier": "flex"}   # cheaper, higher latency
)
```

## Gotcha
Veo and Lyria preview endpoints require the `v1beta` API path — if you're hitting 404s, check that your SDK version is ≥ 1.15.0 (`pip install --upgrade google-genai`) and that your project has the `Generative Language API` enabled in Cloud Console.

learn.name: ml-intern
learn.oneLineDescription: Autonomous ML agent that researches, fine-tunes, and ships Hugging Face models without babysitting.

detail.whatItDoes:
ml-intern is an open-source agent that operates as an autonomous ML engineer inside the Hugging Face ecosystem. Given a natural-language task — 'fine-tune a sentiment classifier on this dataset' or 'find and benchmark the best small model for legal NER' — it reads relevant papers, hunts down HF datasets, writes training code, runs fine-tuning in a sandbox (up to 300 agentic iterations), uploads training traces to a private HF dataset, and pushes model weights to HF Hub when done.

It exposes two modes: interactive chat for exploration, and single-prompt headless execution for fully autonomous runs. Every agent run produces a debuggable, shareable session trace on Hugging Face — not a vanished terminal session. Approval gates are built in for sensitive operations like pushing to Hub or deleting datasets.
detail.whoItsFor: ML engineers and researchers who spend the back half of their time on repetitive fine-tuning, dataset search, and benchmarking tasks rather than novel modeling. Also useful for small teams that want to run overnight ML experiments without building custom orchestration.
pros: Full HF ecosystem integration — datasets, models, training traces all land in your HF account automatically
Session traces are replayable HF datasets, not vanished shell logs — every run is auditable
Headless single-prompt mode works well in CI/CD for scheduled fine-tuning jobs
Built-in approval gates prevent accidental writes to production Hub repos
cons: 300-iteration cap means very long fine-tuning jobs may not complete end-to-end in one run
Tightly coupled to HF ecosystem — less useful if your model registry or data is elsewhere
GPU compute costs are still your problem; the agent doesn't provision infra
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Python 3.10+
- A Hugging Face account with a write-access token (`HF_TOKEN`)
- GPU access recommended for fine-tuning (local, Lambda, or RunPod); CPU works for benchmarking tasks

## Install

```bash
# Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/huggingface/ml-intern
cd ml-intern

# Install dependencies
pip install -e .
```

## Configure

```bash
export HF_TOKEN="hf_your_token_here"
export HF_USERNAME="your-hf-username"   # traces and weights upload here

# Optional: set a default model provider (defaults to HF Inference API)
export ML_INTERN_PROVIDER="openai"       # or "anthropic", "hf"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
```

## Interactive mode

```bash
python -m ml_intern chat

# Inside the chat:
# > Find the best small (<1B) English sentiment model on HF and benchmark it on SST-2
# > Fine-tune distilbert-base-uncased on my dataset hf://datasets/my-org/reviews
```

## Headless single-prompt execution

```bash
# Fully autonomous — runs until done or 300 iterations
python -m ml_intern run \
  "Fine-tune microsoft/deberta-v3-small on glue/mrpc for 3 epochs. \
   Push weights to $HF_USERNAME/deberta-mrpc-finetuned."

# Watch progress — traces upload to HF as they accumulate
# https://huggingface.co/datasets/$HF_USERNAME/ml-intern-traces
```

## Run a benchmark-only task (no GPU needed)

```bash
python -m ml_intern run \
  "Compare the top 5 English NER models under 500M params on CoNLL-2003. \
   Report F1, latency on CPU, and model size."
```

## Gotcha
The agent's default approval gate **will pause and ask you before pushing anything to HF Hub**. If you're running headless in CI and want fully non-interactive behavior, set `ML_INTERN_AUTO_APPROVE=hub_push` in your env — but be careful: this also auto-approves dataset writes. Scope it narrowly.
